title: Agent interfaces become stateful operating layers
summary: Coding agents and browser agents are converging on the same requirement: durable state across sessions and real actions. Session recovery, credentials, approvals and local memory are becoming part of the product surface.
thesis: Agent interfaces are becoming stateful operating layers.

items.name: OpenCode
items.what: Restores ACP session model, effort, mode and reasoning chunk boundaries when loading, resuming or forking sessions, and requests summarized adaptive thinking for GitHub Copilot models.
items.whyDifferent: It treats session continuity as part of the coding-agent interface, reducing state loss when work is resumed or forked across clients.

items.name: Aside
items.price: Free $0 forever; Pro $20/month; Max $200/month; Enterprise contact sales
items.what: A browser agent that works across logged-in websites, local files and communications while keeping credentials out of the model and gating sensitive actions for confirmation.
items.whyDifferent: It combines credentialed browser execution, local memory and approval controls in the browser itself instead of depending on per-service integrations.

readThrough: Teams now need to evaluate how agent systems preserve state across sessions and real actions, not only how well a model answers. Session recovery, credentials, approvals and local memory become product-level requirements when agents operate inside production workflows.
